title.narrative: 1.1 An enabling legal environment for effective implementation of NRA Act, 2019 is created and sustained

description.narrative: 1.1 An enabling legal environment for effective implementation of NRA Act, 2019 is created and sustained

title.narrative: No. of laws and regulations enacted

description.narrative: No. of laws and regulations enacted

comment.narrative: The two laws targeted by the Action namely the guidelines and regulations operationalizing the NRA 2019 the guidelines and regulations operationalizing the Secretariat were enacted and their implementation initiated..1.The Action support the Ministry of Law and Justice to develop guidelines and regulations operationalizing the NRA 2019 Act creating the NRA as a legal entity with legal instruments to discharge their mandate. The guidelines and regulations were approved by cabinet and enacted by Parliament in 2020.2.The NRA 2019 Act was promulgated into law and became effective with the adoption and enactment of the antecedent regulations and gazettement of NRA Members in February 2020.3.The two legislations protected the NRA and insulated it from interference by external parties enabling them to discharge their mandate effectively.4.The Action support policy advisory and technical engagement resulting in production of a Cabinet Memorandum C3202210174 by the Minister of Finance seeking a legal framework for a Transitional Office on Reforms to ensure successful completion of any outstanding work including drafting of enabling legislations structures and systems as well as a framework for peacebuilding and national cohesion.5.The Action supported highlevel policy engagement leading to Cabinet Decision approving the establishment of The National Reforms Transitional Office within the Ministry of Law and Justice to ensure successful completion and coordination of any outstanding work on reforms.Challenges1. There was a delay in finalization and adoption of the NRA Guidelines and Regulations resulting in the prolonged stay in operationalization of the Secretariat.2. Prolonged deliberations and lack of clear succession arrangements leading to dissolution of the NRA without proper transitional arrangements compounded by litigation caused delay in agreement on succession structures for the NRA hence the 4 months hiatus after the lapse of NRA Mandate

The two laws targeted by the Action namely the guidelines and regulations operationalizing the NRA 2019 the guidelines and regulations operationalizing the Secretariat were enacted and their implementation initiated. In addition the Cabinet Memorandum C3202210174 granting a legal framework for the national Reforms Transitional Office was adopted by Cabinet in may 2022.1.The Action support the Ministry of Law and Justice to develop guidelines and regulations operationalizing the NRA 2019 Act creating the NRA as a legal entity with legal instruments to discharge their mandate. The guidelines and regulations were approved by cabinet and enacted by Parliament in 2020.2.The NRA 2019 Act was promulgated into law and became effective with the adoption and enactment of the antecedent regulations and gazettement of NRA Members in February 2020.3.The two legislations protected the NRA and insulated it from interference by external parties enabling them to discharge their mandate effectively.4.The Action support policy advisory and technical engagement resulting in production of a Cabinet Memorandum C3202210174 by the Minister of Finace seeking a legal framework for a Transitional Office on Reforms to ensure successful completion of any outstanding work including drafting of enabling legislations structures and systems as well as a framework for peacebuilding and national cohesion.5.The Action supported highlevel policy engagement leading to Cabinet Decision approving the establishment of The National Reforms Transitional Office within the Ministry of Law and Justice to ensure successful completion and coordination of any outstanding work on reforms.

title.narrative: 1.2 The NRA Secretariat has been established and operationalized

description.narrative: 1.2 The NRA Secretariat has been established and operationalized

title.narrative: No. of operational manuals developed

description.narrative: No. of operational manuals developed

comment.narrative: The Annual Output targets were fully achieved where three operational manuals and five recruitment guidelines were developed approved by the NRA and used to hire the Secretariat Staff. The technical component of this support was undertaken prior to 1.11.2020 however the draft products were reviewed adapted approved and used after the NRA Secretariat was constituted with the recruitment and deployment of the NRA Secretariat. Specifically5.The Terms of Reference were developed advertised and used to procure the Institute of Development Management to provide technical assistance to the Ministry of Law Constitutional Affairs and Human Rights resulting in a Review of the NRA Act 2019 proposition of an organisational structure of the NRA Secretariat including staffing configurations administrative guidelines and remuneration structure consistent with the Public Finance Management regulations b Elaboration of the Terms of Reference for the Secretariat and development of the Job Descriptions as well as person specifications for the senior management technical and operational staff of the NRA Secretariat c Development of recruitment guidelines proposition of selection procedures and the executive selection for the senior management of the NRA Secretariat d Development of the performance measurement system and methods as well as the reporting framework for the NRA Secretariat and e The induction of NRA management technical and operational staff with joint sessions involving NRA Members including clarifying roles and responsibilities6.The Organisational structure of the NRA Secretariat staffing configurations administrative guidelines and remuneration structure was produced and adopted by the NRA Plenary.7.The Terms of Reference Job Descriptions and person specifications for the senior management technical and operational staff of the NRA Secretariat were developed and adopted by the NRA Plenary for use.8.The recruitment guidelines and selection procedures were developed approve and adopted by the NRA Plenary.9.The executive selection process was completed resulting in the recruitment of the Chief and Deputy Executive Officers and operationalization of the Secretariat.10.The Performance measurement system and reporting framework for the NRA Secretariat developed and adopted by the NRA Plenary.

Specifically5.The Terms of Reference were developed advertised and used to procure the Institute of Development Management to provide technical assistance to the Ministry of Law Constitutional Affairs and Human Rights resulting in a Review of the NRA Act 2019 proposition of an organisational structure of the NRA Secretariat including staffing configurations administrative guidelines and remuneration structure consistent with the Public Finance Management regulations b Elaboration of the Terms of Reference for the Secretariat and development of the Job Descriptions as well as person specifications for the senior management technical and operational staff of the NRA Secretariat c Development of recruitment guidelines proposition of selection procedures and the executive selection for the senior management of the NRA Secretariat d Development of the performance measurement system and methods as well as the reporting framework for the NRA Secretariat and e The induction of NRA management technical and operational staff with joint sessions involving NRA Members including clarifying roles and responsibilities6.The Organisational structure of the NRA Secretariat staffing configurations administrative guidelines and remuneration structure was produced and adopted by the NRA Plenary.7.The Terms of Reference Job Descriptions and person specifications for the senior management technical and operational staff of the NRA Secretariat were developed and adopted by the NRA Plenary for use.8.The recruitment guidelines and selection procedures were developed approve and adopted by the NRA Plenary.9.The executive selection process was completed resulting in the recruitment of the Chief and Deputy Executive Officers and operationalization of the Secretariat.10.The Performance measurement system and reporting framework for the NRA Secretariat developed and adopted by the NRA Plenary.

title.narrative: 1.3 The NRAs operational and technical capacity to execute its mandate is enhanced.

description.narrative: 1.3 The NRAs operational and technical capacity to execute its mandate is enhanced.

title.narrative: Proportion of budgeted resources mobilised

description.narrative: Proportion of budgeted resources mobilised

comment.narrative: The Annual Output target was exceeded with 53 of the anticipated resources mobilized and deployed and 100 of the required equipment procured. Specifically1.The Support to Implementation of Lesotho National Reforms Programme Document was formulated quality assured successfully appraised by the Local Project Appraisal Committee and certified as compliant to the Government NRA and stakeholders beneficiary Delegation of European Union Funding Agency and UNDP requirements. 2.The European Union Contribution Agreement with UNDP for EUR2500000.00 was signed on 5th October 2021 with a retroactive commencement date of 1st November 2020.3.A total of EUR1400000.00 was disbursed to UNDP as the First Tranche for implementation of activities under the Support to Implementation of Lesotho National Reforms Programme.4.The key equipment and tools required by the NRA Secretariat including computers printers stationary zoom license were procured and deployed to the Secretariat. 5.A total of EUR800000.00 was disbursed to UNDP as the Second Tranche for the implementation of activities under the Support to Implementation of Lesotho National Reforms Programme.Challenges1 There was a delay in acquisition of office space for the NRA Secretariat which impacted on the activities of the Secretariat that required physical office space to execute.2. EUR300000 was withheld from the Second Tranche disbursement ostensibly because 70 delivery of the First Tranche had not been attained by the reporting period October 31 2021

The Annual Output target was exceeded with 53 of the anticipated resources mobilized and deployed and 100 of the required equipment procured. comment.narrative: The Annual Output target was exceeded with 53 of the anticipated resources mobilized and deployed and 100 of the required equipment procured. Specifically1.The Support to Implementation of Lesotho National Reforms Programme Document was formulated quality assured successfully appraised by the Local Project Appraisal Committee and certified as compliant to the Government NRA and stakeholders beneficiary Delegation of European Union Funding Agency and UNDP requirements. 2.The European Union Contribution Agreement with UNDP for EUR2500000.00 was signed on 5th October 2021 with a retroactive commencement date of 1st November 2020.3.A total of EUR1400000.00 was disbursed to UNDP as the First Tranche for implementation of activities under the Support to Implementation of Lesotho National Reforms Programme.4.The key equipment and tools required by the NRA Secretariat including computers printers stationary zoom license were procured and deployed to the Secretariat. 5.A total of EUR800000.00 was disbursed to UNDP as the Second Tranche for the implementation of activities under the Support to Implementation of Lesotho National Reforms Programme.Challenges1 There was a delay in acquisition of office space for the NRA Secretariat which impacted on the activities of the Secretariat that required physical office space to execute.2. EUR300000 was withheld from the Second Tranche disbursement ostensibly because 70 delivery of the First Tranche had not been attained by the reporting period October 31 2021

comment.narrative: The Annual Output target was partially met by 31 October 2021 as follows1.The Terms of Reference for the Secretariat Job Descriptions as well as person specifications for the senior management technical and operational staff of the NRA Secretariat were developed and adopted by the NRA Plenary.2.A total of 31 staff 1 Chief Executive Officer 1 Deputy Chief Executive Officer 4 Thematic Sector Advisors 4 Chief Officers Legal Finance Human Resources and Public Relations 2 Legal Drafters 3 Officers Accountant IT and HRAdministration 7 Reforms Clerks and 9 Support Staff3.A Cabinet decision establishing a National Reforms Transitional Office within the Ministry of Justice and Law was approved and a request for support was activated. The Office developed a programme of work to sustain the reforms with a funding request to complement the Governments contribution.Challenges1 The NRA technical capacity was highly impacted by the delay in deployment of Experts as well identification and recruitment of qualified personnel locally and internationally. Experts who were to be deployed as part of the technical contribution from the Commonwealth Secretariat were not availed in time resulting in nonrecruitment and deployment of 2 technical Advisors parliamentary and public service. 2 Additionally the resignation of two technical staff caused a variance in the number of personnel required to be maintained in the post at the Secretariat.3 There were prolonged negotiations on the Terms and Conditions of Service of the NRA Secretariat resulting in the onimplementation of activities related to capacity building of civil service staff undertaking of analysis and policy studies.4 Prolonged deliberations and lack of clear succession arrangements leading to the dissolution of the NRA without active transitional arrangements compounded by litigation caused a delay in agreement on succession structures for the NRA hence the 4 months hiatus after the lapse of the NRA Mandate.5. In October 2022 a decision to suspend the Action following the court decision on the 10th Amendment to the Constitution Bill 2022 altered the implementation arrangement of activities related to the maintenance of staff at post.6. Whereas a request to extend support to the National Reforms Transitional Office was advanced in May 2022 the nonpassage of the 10th Amendment to the Constitution Bill 2022 meant that the proposed activities such as enabling legislations and establishments of new institutions proposed in the Amendment could not be legally implemented.

comment.narrative: The Annual Output Target was partially fulfilled through the completion of preparatory activities necessary to recruit and deploy technical advisors as follows1.The Terms of Reference for the Secretariat Job Descriptions as well as person specifications for the senior management technical and operational staff of the NRA Secretariat were developed and adopted by the NRA Plenary.2.4 out of 7 thematic experts were identified and recruited to support thematic sectors. They include 1 Security Sector Expert 1 Media Sector Expert 1 Economic Sector Expert and 1 Justice Sector Expert.3.The experts provided technical support and advise to NRA subcommittees resulting in production of 98 pieces of legislation and constitutional amendments were processed by NRA submitted to the Minister of Law and Justice approved by cabinet and tabled in parliaments through the Omnibus Bill. The Omnibus Bill went through the first reading and was presented to the Parliamentary Portfolio Committee for scrutiny

comment.narrative: 1 The activities under the output were significantly affected by lack of funding. Whereas UNDP had agreed to prefinance the Contribution Agreement the limited funds from UNDP could not sufficiently cover the planned expenditures for a prolonged period of time. The limited funds were diverted to priority costs particularly salaries emoluments and equipment for the NRA Secretariat 2. Following the October 2022 general elections that brought in a new Government a decision was reached to suspend the Institutional Gap Analysis to ensure that the process is aligned to the vision and strategic objective of the new Government. This was done to ensure buyin but also immediate utility of the products to support strategic priorities of the new Government. As result the assignment completion was delay by a further 8 months.

title.narrative: 2.3 Policy studies, analysis, costing and legislative drafting in the seven thematic sectors

description.narrative: 2.3 Policy studies, analysis, costing and legislative drafting in the seven thematic sectors

title.narrative: No. of studies, analyses, costings commissioned

description.narrative: No. of studies, analyses, costings commissioned

comment.narrative: Limited progress was made towards the achievement of the annual targets. The activity is pegged on the passage of the Omnibus Bill. Technical consultations are ongoing on the nature and frame of the costing process in terms of thematic or sectoral costing. Specifically1.Strategic level discussions are ongoing with the Comptroller of Budget on the structure and approach of the costing exercise resulting in the identification of the macroeconomist that shall lead in the development of the costing model and indices for use in the final analysis.2.Consultations with the African Development Bank and the World Bank have also been initiated to provide technical expertise in the construction of the costing model and outputs.3.As part of the Institutional Gap Assessment a component of Conceptualization design and production of an institutional capacity development project document to support the operationalization of the comprehensive implementable institutional capacity development programme for the National Assembly Parliament and Senate Judiciary and The Executive Office of the Prime Minister Ministries of Justice and Law Development Planning Foreign Affairs and International Relations Defence and National Security and Police and Public Safety in delivering on agreed national reforms was initiated in August 2022 and is ongoing. Challenges1 The activities under the output were significantly affected by lack of funding. Whereas UNDP had agreed to prefinance the Contribution Agreement the limited funds available could not sufficiently cover all the planned expenditures. comment.narrative: 1.Limited progress was achieved in the specific activity due to insufficient funds from the prefinancing arrangement. To fasttrack implementation lead Civil Society Organizations have been identified to agree on selection criteria call for proposals and capacity building programme for the grantees.2.However Preparatory work for convening the First HighLevel Forum on Implementation of Lesotho National Reforms geared towards adequately informing stakeholders and the Basotho public about national reforms implementation process provide space for national reflection and forward looking were initiated. These included conceptualisation of the Forum securing venue developing communication and visibility materials and securing high level political concurrence on the public value and legitimacy of the event. 3.A perception survey is planned for March 2022 is purposively identified to coincide with the High Level Forum on Implementation of Reforms that is expected to have a broad cross section of stakeholders local and SADC over a period of 3 days to collect missing data.

comment.narrative: 1.Limited progress was achieved in the specific activity due to insufficient funds from the prefinancing arrangement. To fasttrack implementation lead Civil Society Organizations have been identified to agree on selection criteria call for proposals and capacity building programme for the grantees.2.However Preparatory work for convening the First HighLevel Forum on Implementation of Lesotho National Reforms geared towards adequately informing stakeholders and the Basotho public about national reforms implementation process provide space for national reflection and forward looking were initiated. These included conceptualization of the Forum securing venue developing communication and visibility materials and securing high level political concurrence on the public value and legitimacy of the event. 3.A perception survey is planned for March 2022 is purposively identified to coincide with the High Level Forum on Implementation of Reforms that is expected to have a broad cross section of stakeholders local and SADC over a period of 3 days to collect missing data.4.The First HighLevel Forum on the State of the Implementation of the Lesotho National Reforms was successfully held in May 2022. The Forum provided an opportunity to take stock and agree on an accelerated mechanism for fasttracking the processing of the Omnibus Bill and a way forward on transitional arrangements for the reforms process post NRA. Key outcomes were a acknowledgement and agreement on arrangements for resuscitating component C of the national reforms agenda that seeks to achieve Sustainable Peace National Unity and Reconciliation that is national b agreement on interim measures for sustained implementation of the national reforms that paved the way for the establishment of the National Reforms Transitional Office c agreement on the work programme for the transitional arrangements and an outcome document on bipartisan approach to processing of the Omnibus Bill including workshop sessions for legislators to achieve collective consensus on the form and contents of the Bill httpswww.gov.lsdownloadhighlevelforumonthestateoftheimplementationofthelesothonationalreforms httpslesotho.un.orgen177156highlevelforumstatusimplementationlesothonationalreforms 5.To enhance citizen participation in national processes the Programme in collaboration with key stakeholders generated key priorities for capacity development that will improve citizen engagement in the implementation of the national reforms httpswww.undp.org. The consensus building process led by the CSOs resulted in agreement at the Senate and National Assembly leading to passage of the 11th Constitutional Amendment through extraordinary recall of parliament.6.To ensure equal and effective participation of women in the reforms implementation process Women were supported to translate the Womens position paper to the national dialogue into a legislative and policy agenda to inform the translation of the MultiStakeholder National Dialogue and Plenary II report into 10th Constitutional Amendment. This resulted in mainstreaming women and gender issues into the 10th Amendment and subsequent Bills. Of the 98 Amendments 46 directly address women and gender issues such as the age of majority public appointments electoral process inheritance justice reforms and security sector practices that were discriminatory to women. Additionally direct measures were supported to ensure youth people with disabilities the elderly and other marginalized issues were prioritized and consolidated into the 11th Constitutional Amendment

The consensus building process led by the CSOs resulted in agreement at the Senate and National Assembly leading to passage of the 11th Constitutional Amendment through extraordinary recall of parliament.6.To ensure equal and effective participation of women in the reforms implementation process Women were supported to translate the Womens position paper to the national dialogue into a legislative and policy agenda to inform the translation of the MultiStakeholder National Dialogue and Plenary II report into 10th Constitutional Amendment. This resulted in mainstreaming women and gender issues into the 10th Amendment and subsequent Bills. Of the 98 Amendments 46 directly address women and gender issues such as the age of majority public appointments electoral process inheritance justice reforms and security sector practices that were discriminatory to women. Additionally direct measures were supported to ensure youth people with disabilities the elderly and other marginalized issues were prioritized and consolidated into the 11th Constitutional Amendment

The results achieved include the following1.I communication and media strategy for the NRA was produced and approved by the NRA Plenary for implementation.2.Radio and TV campaign programme was developed and adopted for implementation with regular TV appearances by NRA Members and Secretariat.3.Flyers brochures burners billboards and branded stationary were designed and awaiting reproduction and dissemination.4.Regular newspaper articles and paid advertisements were generated and disseminated in weekly publications.5.The NRA was supported to design develop produce and disseminate a regular radio and TV programmmes on reforms newspaper articles flyers and brochures burners and billboards and branded stationary in addition to electronic running screens in shopping malls and production of the NRA Annual Progress ReportChallenges1 The activities under the output were significantly affected by lack of funding. Whereas UNDP had agreed to prefinance the Contribution Agreement the limited funds could not sufficiently cover the planned expenditures for a prolonged period. The limited funds were diverted to priority activities particularly salaries emoluments and equipment for the NRA Secretariat.2 In October 2022 a decision to suspend the Action following the court decision on the 10th Amendment to the Constitution Bill 2022 altered the implementation arrangement of some activities related to developing produce and disseminate information education and communication materials on implementation of reforms.

Limited progress was achieved in the specific activity owing to limited funding from prefinancing facility. title.narrative: 5.1 Mobilization and deployment of strategic programme personnel and staffing

description.narrative: 5.1 Mobilization and deployment of strategic programme personnel and staffing

title.narrative: No. of strategic personnel recruited

description.narrative: No. of strategic personnel recruited

comment.narrative: The Annual Output targets were partially met as follows.1.The Terms of Reference for Programme Manager Driver Communications Monitoring and Evaluations Specialist Project Analyst and Finance and Administration Officer were reviewed and new ones were developed.2.A total of 3 staff were recruited and deployed at post namely Programme Manager Driver Finance and Administration Officer 3.The post of Communications Monitoring and Evaluations Specialist was advertised and a suitable candidate was offered the position.4.Annual Performance Appraisal of staff is earmarked for February 2022.5.Following the competitive recruitment for the post of Communications Monitoring and Evaluations Specialist the selected candidate declined the offer due to personal reasons considering the remainder of the period 10 months a decision was made to engage an already serving UNDP staff from the Malawi Country Office under the Detailed Assignment modality. The staff served for 4 months.6.Annual Performance Appraisal of staff was undertaken in February 2022 which found 2 staffs performance were satisfactory and 1 staff exceeded expectations.Challenges1 The activities under the output were significantly affected by lack of funding. Whereas UNDP had agreed to prefinance the Contribution Agreement the limited funds could not sufficiently cover the planned expenditures for a prolonged period. The limited funds were diverted to priority activities particularly salaries emoluments and equipment for the NRA Secretariat.2 Since UNDP recruitment procedures require a confirmation of availability of funds by way of existing active Charts of Accounts with sufficient funds to initiate the recruitment process UNDP was constrained to proceed with the recruitment due to the prolonged negotiations that impacted available funds. 3 The activities related to communication and public awareness were slowed down due to the nonavailability of the staff and funds to implement the activities. 4 The two positions of Programme Analyst and Communications Monitoring and Evaluations Specialist were not filled and maintained at post due to the aftermath of COVID19 restrictions. When the restrictions were lifted the identified candidate declined the offer and the recruitment process could not be reintroduced due to the limited duration of the Programme.5 In October 2022 the general elections that ushered in a new government were held. This was followed by the reorganization of Government Functions including the amalgamation of Ministries new appointments of Ministers and technical changes that called for realignment of Programme Management ArrangementStructures with the new framework. Additionally it required securing appointments and briefing of the new leadership. As a result the Second Biannual Board Meeting could not be held at the scheduled period of DecemberJanuary

1.The Terms of Reference for Programme Manager Driver Communications Monitoring and Evaluations Specialist Project Analyst and Finance and Administration Officer were reviewed and new ones were developed.2.A total of 3 staff were recruited and deployed at post namely Programme Manager Driver Finance and Administration Officer 3.The post of Communications Monitoring and Evaluations Specialist was advertised and a suitable candidate was offered the position.4.Annual Performance Appraisal of staff is earmarked for February 2022.5.Following the competitive recruitment for the post of Communications Monitoring and Evaluations Specialist the selected candidate declined the offer due to personal reasons considering the remainder of the period 10 months a decision was made to engage an already serving UNDP staff from the Malawi Country Office under the Detailed Assignment modality. The staff served for 4 months.6.Annual Performance Appraisal of staff was undertaken in February 2022 which found 2 staffs performance were satisfactory and 1 staff exceeded expectations.

This was followed by the reorganization of Government Functions including the amalgamation of Ministries new appointments of Ministers and technical changes that called for realignment of Programme Management ArrangementStructures with the new framework. Additionally it required securing appointments and briefing of the new leadership. As a result the Second Biannual Board Meeting could not be held at the scheduled period of DecemberJanuary

1.The Terms of Reference for Programme Manager Driver Communications Monitoring and Evaluations Specialist Project Analyst and Finance and Administration Officer were reviewed and new ones were developed.2.A total of 3 staff were recruited and deployed at post namely Programme Manager Driver Finance and Administration Officer 3.The post of Communications Monitoring and Evaluations Specialist was advertised and a suitable candidate was offered the position.4.Annual Performance Appraisal of staff is earmarked for February 2022.5.Following the competitive recruitment for the post of Communications Monitoring and Evaluations Specialist the selected candidate declined the offer due to personal reasons considering the remainder of the period 10 months a decision was made to engage an already serving UNDP staff from the Malawi Country Office under the Detailed Assignment modality. The staff served for 4 months.6.Annual Performance Appraisal of staff was undertaken in February 2022 which found 2 staffs performance were satisfactory and 1 staff exceeded expectations.

title.narrative: 5.2 Monitoring of, reporting on and evaluation the programme

description.narrative: 5.2 Monitoring of, reporting on and evaluation the programme

title.narrative: No. of Programme reports produced

description.narrative: No. of Programme reports produced

comment.narrative: 1.Annual Programme Monitoring and Evaluation Plan was developed and uploaded in ATLAS as part of the Description of Action.2.A Project Risk Log was developed uploaded in ATLAS and updated biannually.3.GovernmentNRAEuropean Union UNDP highlevel platform was established with a regular rhythm of meetings held quarterly.4.Highlevel policy engagement was convened with actionable recommendations including consultations with the SADC Facilitation Team Parliamentary Portfolio Committees.5.Preparatory work towards the First HighLevel Forum on Implementation of The Lesotho National Reforms was completed seeking to adequately inform stakeholders and the Basotho public about the activities and expected results of the programme. It shall ensure a wide engagement of key targeted stakeholders and present targeted consistent messages of the programme.6.1 Programme Board and Programme Implementation Committee Meeting was held to approve the programme document annual work plan and budget. The Programme Board and Programme Implementation Committee held in February 2020 also served as the Local Project Appraisal Committee in line with the UNDP Programmes and Operation Policies and Procedures.7.2 programme review meetings were held and programme progress was presented to stakeholders.8.UNDP internal meetings were held weekly to review progress and biweekly to review programme performance and compliance.9.Risks identified during the design and initiation such as prolonged negotiations and lack of consensus on the implementation of the reforms were routinely monitored and mitigated. These included the events surrounding the lapse of the NRA mandate delayed enactment of the 10th Amendment to the Constitution Bill 2022 the declaration of the state of emergency and the litigation thereafter. Upon consultation a decision was reached to suspend the Action on an exceptional basis with six months period of minimum costs.10.Sustained highlevel policy consultation with the Government EU and stakeholders continued during the implementation period. Key results include the content generation for the Cabinet Memorandum establishing the National Reforms Transitional Office and the programme of work concurrence on the exceptional suspension of the Action with enabling conditions to keep the Action alive and continued engagement on the reforms process.11.The 2nd Annual Progress Report 2021 2022 with Financial Annex was produced for submission to the Board. Challenges
1st Annual Progress Report 1 November 2020 31 October 2021 Support to Implementation of Lesotho National Reforms Programme FED2021422688.

Upon consultation a decision was reached to suspend the Action on an exceptional basis with six months period of minimum costs.10.Sustained highlevel policy consultation with the Government EU and stakeholders continued during the implementation period. Key results include the content generation for the Cabinet Memorandum establishing the National Reforms Transitional Office and the programme of work concurrence on the exceptional suspension of the Action with enabling conditions to keep the Action alive and continued engagement on the reforms process.11.The 2nd Annual Progress Report 2021 2022 with Financial Annex was produced for submission to the Board. title.narrative: Proportion of financial resources and equipment of the total projected budget: delivered/ absorbed

description.narrative: Proportion of financial resources and equipment of the total projected budget: delivered/ absorbed

comment.narrative: 1.The Support to Implementation of Lesotho National Reforms Programme Document was formulated quality assured successfully appraised by the Local Project Appraisal Committee and certified as compliant to the Government NRA and stakeholders beneficiary Delegation of European Union Funding Agency and UNDP requirements. 2.The European Union Contribution Agreement with UNDP for EUR2500000.00 was signed on 5th October 2021 with a retroactive commencement date of 1st November 2020 with a UNDP commitment of 448097.00 contribution.3.A total of EUR1400000.00 was disbursed to UNDP as the First Tranche the implementation of activities under the Support to Implementation of Lesotho National Reforms Programme while UNDPs contribution is estimated at 140000.00 a total of 1540000.00 or 52 of the total budget was realized during the first year of implementation4.A comprehensively consolidated justification was prepared to request for a second prefinancing instalment resulting in concurrence from the Delegation of the European Union and disbursement of a total of 863900.38 with an outstanding amount of 236099.62 that was withheld by application of the provisions of Article 19.1iii of the Contribution Agreement. These funds shall be requested once the threshold is reached.5.Upon suspension of the Action by the Delegation of the European Union as a result of nullification of the 10th Amendment to the Constitution Act 2022. highly convincing arguments were grafted resulting in concurrence from the Delegation of the European Union to implement minimum activities that have sustained engagement with the Government attained Government commitment to the reforms and positively UNDP as a convenor thought leader and policy broker in the national reforms process. 6.As part of sustainability continuity and resource mobilization the programme continued developing background materials for policy engagement with the Government Donors and other partners as well as concept notes including the US17Million UNWide concept paper on Improved Governance for Optimized Public Service Delivery In Lesotho that seeks to achieve efficient service delivery to all Basotho through four interrelated initiatives 1 effective leadership and management of the public sector 2 efficient and informed resource allocation and utilization 3 establishing egovernance for enhanced accessibility to government services and 4 institutionalizing an accountability mechanism. The concept paper has received acclaim interest and support from UNCT the World Bank Government and Development Partners.

comment.narrative: 1.The Support to Implementation of Lesotho National Reforms Programme Document was formulated quality assured successfully appraised by the Local Project Appraisal Committee and certified as compliant to the Government NRA and stakeholders beneficiary Delegation of European Union Funding Agency and UNDP requirements. 2.The European Union Contribution Agreement with UNDP for EUR2500000.00 was signed on 5th October 2021 with a retroactive commencement date of 1st November 2020 with a UNDP commitment of 448097.00 contribution.3.A total of EUR1400000.00 was disbursed to UNDP as the First Tranche the implementation of activities under the Support to Implementation of Lesotho National Reforms Programme while UNDPs contribution is estimated at 140000.00 a total of 1540000.00 or 52 of the total budget was realized during the first year of implementation4.A comprehensively consolidated justification was prepared to request for a second prefinancing instalment resulting in concurrence from the Delegation of the European Union and disbursement of a total of 863900.38 with an outstanding amount of 236099.62 that was withheld by application of the provisions of Article 19.1iii of the Contribution Agreement. These funds shall be requested once the threshold is reached.5.Upon suspension of the Action by the Delegation of the European Union as a result of nullification of the 10th Amendment to the Constitution Act 2022. highly convincing arguments were grafted resulting in concurrence from the Delegation of the European Union to implement minimum activities that have sustained engagement with the Government attained Government commitment to the reforms and positively UNDP as a convenor thought leader and policy broker in the national reforms process. 6.As part of sustainability continuity and resource mobilization the programme continued developing background materials for policy engagement with the Government Donors and other partners as well as concept notes including the US17Million UNWide concept paper on Improved Governance for Optimized Public Service Delivery In Lesotho that seeks to achieve efficient service delivery to all Basotho through four interrelated initiatives 1 effective leadership and management of the public sector 2 efficient and informed resource allocation and utilization 3 establishing egovernance for enhanced accessibility to government services and 4 institutionalizing an accountability mechanism. The concept paper has received acclaim interest and support from UNCT the World Bank Government and Development Partners.

1.The Support to Implementation of Lesotho National Reforms Programme Document was formulated quality assured successfully appraised by the Local Project Appraisal Committee and certified as compliant to the Government NRA and stakeholders beneficiary Delegation of European Union Funding Agency and UNDP requirements. 2.The European Union Contribution Agreement with UNDP for EUR2500000.00 was signed on 5th October 2021 with a retroactive commencement date of 1st November 2020 with a UNDP commitment of 448097.00 contribution.3.A total of EUR1400000.00 was disbursed to UNDP as the First Tranche for implementation of activities under the Support to Implementation of Lesotho National Reforms Programme while UNDPs contribution is estimated at 140000.00 a total of 1540000.00 or 52 of the total budget was realized during the first year of implementation

title.narrative: 3.0 Enhanced citizen participation in the implementation of national reforms

description.narrative: Civil society organisations, gender and youth groups, people living with disabilities and other special interest groups shall be supported to organise, articulate their issues and effectively participate in the implementation of the reforms process. Their capacity to identify monitorable issues, monitor implementation and raise concerns will be enhanced. In collaboration with the Lesotho Council of NonGovernmental Organisations and the Christian Council of Lesotho, specific platforms will be established and supported to ensure continuous dialogue to ensure that their representative on the National Reforms Authority are better prepared to present respective position and productively engage with other members and the state. Through commissioned studies on specific issues, knowledge will be gathered and generated to ensure informed positions are articulated to leave no one behind. A mechanism for sustained consensus building will be created to diffuse potential conflicts that could derail the reforms. Ongoing conversation on national reconciliation processes will be supported to address retrospective areas of injustice including the establishment of legal and institutional framework thereof

comment.narrative: 1.Limited progress was achieved in the specific activity due to insufficient funds from the prefinancing arrangement. To fasttrack implementation lead Civil Society Organizations have been identified to agree on selection criteria call for proposals and capacity building programme for the grantees.2.However Preparatory work for convening the First HighLevel Forum on Implementation of Lesotho National Reforms geared towards adequately informing stakeholders and the Basotho public about national reforms implementation process provide space for national reflection and forward looking were initiated. These included conceptualization of the Forum securing venue developing communication and visibility materials and securing high level political concurrence on the public value and legitimacy of the event. 3.A perception survey is planned for March 2022 is purposively identified to coincide with the High Level Forum on Implementation of Reforms that is expected to have a broad cross section of stakeholders local and SADC over a period of 3 days to collect missing data.4.The First HighLevel Forum on the State of the Implementation of the Lesotho National Reforms was successfully held in May 2022. The Forum provided an opportunity to take stock and agree on an accelerated mechanism for fasttracking the processing of the Omnibus Bill and a way forward on transitional arrangements for the reforms process post NRA. Key outcomes were a acknowledgement and agreement on arrangements for resuscitating component C of the national reforms agenda that seeks to achieve Sustainable Peace National Unity and Reconciliation that is national b agreement on interim measures for sustained implementation of the national reforms that paved the way for the establishment of the National Reforms Transitional Office c agreement on the work programme for the transitional arrangements and an outcome document on bipartisan approach to processing of the Omnibus Bill including workshop sessions for legislators to achieve collective consensus on the form and contents of the Bill httpswww.gov.lsdownloadhighlevelforumonthestateoftheimplementationofthelesothonationalreforms httpslesotho.un.orgen177156highlevelforumstatusimplementationlesothonationalreforms 5.To enhance citizen participation in national processes the Programme in collaboration with key stakeholders generated key priorities for capacity development that will improve citizen engagement in the implementation of the national reforms httpswww.undp.org. The consensus building process led by the CSOs resulted in agreement at the Senate and National Assembly leading to passage of the 11th Constitutional Amendment through extraordinary recall of parliament.6.To ensure equal and effective participation of women in the reforms implementation process Women were supported to translate the Womens position paper to the national dialogue into a legislative and policy agenda to inform the translation of the MultiStakeholder National Dialogue and Plenary II report into 10th Constitutional Amendment. This resulted in mainstreaming women and gender issues into the 10th Amendment and subsequent Bills. Of the 98 Amendments 46 directly address women and gender issues such as the age of majority public appointments electoral process inheritance justice reforms and security sector practices that were discriminatory to women. Additionally direct measures were supported to ensure youth people with disabilities the elderly and other marginalized issues were prioritized and consolidated into the 11th Constitutional Amendment

1 The activities under the output were significantly affected by lack of funding. Whereas UNDP had agreed to prefinance the Contribution Agreement the limited funds could not sufficiently cover the planned expenditures for a prolonged period. The limited funds were diverted to priority activities particularly salaries emoluments and equipment for the NRA Secretariat2 In October 2022 a decision to suspend the Action following the court decision on the 10th Amendment to the Constitution Bill 2022 altered the implementation arrangement of activities related to Enhanced citizen participation in the implementation of national reforms

title.narrative: Proportion of citizens out of 2,000,000 total population reached

description.narrative: Proportion of citizens out of 2,000,000 total population reached

comment.narrative: 1.Limited progress was achieved in the specific activity due to insufficient funds from the prefinancing arrangement. To fasttrack implementation lead Civil Society Organizations have been identified to agree on selection criteria call for proposals and capacity building programme for the grantees.2.However Preparatory work for convening the First HighLevel Forum on Implementation of Lesotho National Reforms geared towards adequately informing stakeholders and the Basotho public about national reforms implementation process provide space for national reflection and forward looking were initiated. These included conceptualization of the Forum securing venue developing communication and visibility materials and securing high level political concurrence on the public value and legitimacy of the event. 3.A perception survey is planned for March 2022 is purposively identified to coincide with the High Level Forum on Implementation of Reforms that is expected to have a broad cross section of stakeholders local and SADC over a period of 3 days to collect missing data.4.The First HighLevel Forum on the State of the Implementation of the Lesotho National Reforms was successfully held in May 2022. The Forum provided an opportunity to take stock and agree on an accelerated mechanism for fasttracking the processing of the Omnibus Bill and a way forward on transitional arrangements for the reforms process post NRA. Key outcomes were a acknowledgement and agreement on arrangements for resuscitating component C of the national reforms agenda that seeks to achieve Sustainable Peace National Unity and Reconciliation that is national b agreement on interim measures for sustained implementation of the national reforms that paved the way for the establishment of the National Reforms Transitional Office c agreement on the work programme for the transitional arrangements and an outcome document on bipartisan approach to processing of the Omnibus Bill including workshop sessions for legislators to achieve collective consensus on the form and contents of the Bill httpswww.gov.lsdownloadhighlevelforumonthestateoftheimplementationofthelesothonationalreforms httpslesotho.un.orgen177156highlevelforumstatusimplementationlesothonationalreforms 5.To enhance citizen participation in national processes the Programme in collaboration with key stakeholders generated key priorities for capacity development that will improve citizen engagement in the implementation of the national reforms httpswww.undp.org. The consensus building process led by the CSOs resulted in agreement at the Senate and National Assembly leading to passage of the 11th Constitutional Amendment through extraordinary recall of parliament.6.To ensure equal and effective participation of women in the reforms implementation process Women were supported to translate the Womens position paper to the national dialogue into a legislative and policy agenda to inform the translation of the MultiStakeholder National Dialogue and Plenary II report into 10th Constitutional Amendment. This resulted in mainstreaming women and gender issues into the 10th Amendment and subsequent Bills. Of the 98 Amendments 46 directly address women and gender issues such as the age of majority public appointments electoral process inheritance justice reforms and security sector practices that were discriminatory to women. Additionally direct measures were supported to ensure youth people with disabilities the elderly and other marginalized issues were prioritized and consolidated into the 11th Constitutional Amendment

title.narrative: 1.0: The National Reforms Authority/National Reforms Transitional Office is operationalized and effectively discharging its mandate in close collaboration with the Basotho

description.narrative: The National Reforms Authority shall be operational through creation of the required legal framework for the effective establishment and discharge of duties and responsibilities of the Authority. The enabling legal environment entails enactment of the law but also development of regulations, guidelines and supplementary legislations to insulate the Authority from interference. The enabling legal environment shall also provide the Authority with security of tenure to discharge their mandate. In addition to the legal framework, the NRA Secretariat shall be established with the operational capacity to oversee implementation of the reforms. National Reforms Authority with the necessary legitimacy and operational capacity to implement shall be able to deliver the required value of national reforms to all Basotho and transform Lesotho into a stable country.

title.narrative: No. of NRA Technical and Operational Structures operationalized

description.narrative: No. of NRA Technical and Operational Structures operationalized

comment.narrative: The Annual Output targets were fully achieved where three operational manuals and five recruitment guidelines were developed approved by the NRA and used to hire the Secretariat Staff. The Terms of Reference were developed advertised and used to procure the Institute of Development Management to provide technical assistance to the Ministry of Law Constitutional Affairs and Human Rights resulting in a Review of the NRA Act 2019 proposition of an organisational structure of the NRA Secretariat including staffing configurations administrative guidelines and remuneration structure consistent with the Public Finance Management regulations b Elaboration of the Terms of Reference for the Secretariat and development of the Job Descriptions as well as person specifications for the senior management technical and operational staff of the NRA Secretariat c Development of recruitment guidelines proposition of selection procedures and the executive selection for the senior management of the NRA Secretariat d Development of the performance measurement system and methods as well as the reporting framework for the NRA Secretariat and e The induction of NRA management technical and operational staff with joint sessions involving NRA Members including clarifying roles and responsibilities.The Organisational structure of the NRA Secretariat staffing configurations administrative guidelines and remuneration structure was produced and adopted by the NRA Plenary.The Terms of Reference Job Descriptions and person specifications for the senior management technical and operational staff of the NRA Secretariat were developed and adopted by the NRA Plenary for use.The recruitment guidelines and selection procedures were developed approve and adopted by the NRA Plenary.The executive selection process was completed resulting in the recruitment of the Chief and Deputy Executive Officers and operationalization of the Secretariat.The Performance measurement system and reporting framework for the NRA Secretariat developed and adopted by the NRA Plenary.A total of 32 Secretariat staff were recruited deployed and inducted to execute Secretariat functions as follows 4 Thematic Sector Advisors 4 Chief Officers Legal Finance Human Resources and Public Relations 2 Legal Drafters 3 Officers Accountant IT and HRAdministration 7 Reforms Clerks and 9 Support Staff.A Cabinet decision establishing a National Reforms Transitional Office within the Ministry of Justice and Law was approved and a request for support was activated. The Office developed a programme of work to sustain the reforms with a funding request to complement the Governments contribution.The Annual Output target was exceeded with 70 of the anticipated resources mobilized and deployed and 100 of the required equipment procured.

The Output targets were fully achieved by October 2021 as demonstrated by the achievement of milestone targets where the three core structures namely the NRA Plenary the SubCommittees and the Secretariat were constituted established and operationalized. Key impact oriented intervention by the Action include1.Technical and financial support to the Ministry of Law and Justice to develop guidelines and regulations operationalizing the NRA 2019 Act creating the NRA as a legal entity with legal instruments to discharge their mandate. The guidelines and regulations were approved by cabinet and enacted by Parliament in 2020.2.The NRA was gazetted and inaugurated in February 2020 through public swearing in and administering of the Oath of Office administered by the Chief Justice of the Kingdom of Lesotho.3.The NRA developed the organizational structure operational guidelines and tools for the full functioning of the Secretariat. Although the technical support to this activity was undertaken prior to 1.11.2020 the draft products were reviewed adapted and used after the NRA Secretariat was constituted with the recruitment of the CEO and Deputy CEO as per the NRA 2019 Act4.Seven thematic committees were established aligned to the seven thematic sectors of the reforms.5.The Action support the NRA to operationalize the organizational structure operational guidelines and tools by recruiting and deploying the Secretariat personnel. The technical component of this support was undertaken prior to 1.11.2020 however the draft products were reviewed adapted and used after the NRA Secretariat was constituted with the recruitment and deployment of the NRA Secretariat6.Core equipment and tools including computers printers and stationary were procured and delivered to the NRA Secretariat

follows 4 Thematic Sector Advisors 4 Chief Officers Legal Finance Human Resources and Public Relations 2 Legal Drafters 3 Officers Accountant IT and HRAdministration 7 Reforms Clerks and 9 Support Staff.A Cabinet decision establishing a National Reforms Transitional Office within the Ministry of Justice and Law was approved and a request for support was activated. The enabling legal environment entails enactment of the law but also development of regulations, guidelines and supplementary legislations to insulate the Authority from interference. title.narrative: No. of NRA Technical and Operational Structures constituted

description.narrative: No. of NRA Technical and Operational Structures constituted

comment.narrative: The Output targets were fully achieved by October 2021 as demonstrated by the achievement of milestone targets where the three core structures namely the NRA Plenary the SubCommittees and the Secretariat were constituted established and operationalized. An enabling legal environment for the effective implementation of the NRA Act 2019 was created through supplementary legislation regulations and rules that ensured the independence of the Authority. The NRA Secretariat with a staff complement of 31 staff was established to provide technical and operational capacity for the effective functioning of the Authority. Key impactoriented intervention by the Action include1.Technical and financial support to the Ministry of Law and Justice to develop guidelines and regulations operationalizing the NRA 2019 Act creating the NRA as a legal entity with legal instruments to discharge their mandate. The guidelines and regulations were approved by cabinet and enacted by Parliament in 2020.2.The NRA was gazette and inaugurated in February 2020 through public swearing in and administering of the Oath of Office administered by the Chief Justice of the Kingdom of Lesotho.3.The NRA developed the organizational structure operational guidelines and tools for the full functioning of the Secretariat. Although the technical support to this activity was undertaken prior to 1.11.2020 the draft products were reviewed adapted and used after the NRA Secretariat was constituted with the recruitment of the CEO and Deputy CEO as per the NRA 2019 Act4. Seven thematic committees were established aligned to the seven thematic sectors of the reforms.5. The Action supported the NRA to operationalize the organizational structure operational guidelines and tools by recruiting and deploying the Secretariat personnel. The technical component of this support was undertaken prior to 1.11.2020 however the draft products were reviewed adapted and used after the NRA Secretariat was constituted with the recruitment and deployment of the NRA Secretariat6. Core equipment and tools including computers printers and stationery were procured and delivered to the NRA Secretariat.7. Through highlevel policy dialogue and technical engagement Cabinet approved and established a National Reforms Transitional Office within the Ministry of Law and Justice to take over and oversee the completion of outstanding work from the NRA.8.The National Reforms Transitional Office developed and produced a programme of work that was approved by the Ministry and stakeholders. The Office was established for sustainability and continuity inclusive and smooth transitional develop and complete critical and urgent enabling legislation implement the Peace and Transitional Justice mandate propose a new national reforms structure that will succeed the NRA. 9. Key deliverables include development and completion of outstanding Constitutional amendments Development and completion of urgent enabling legislation policies and regulations Providing support to the Honourable Minister of Justice and Law as well as the Relevant Parliamentary Portfolio Committee that is seized with the omnibus Constitutional Bill Development of a draft Workplan for Implementation of the Peace and Reconciliation mandate Development of a proposal for a new reforms structure Reforms implementation sequencing gap analysis and costing Administration issues and winding up of office.Challenges There was a delay in finalization and adoption of the NRA Guidelines and Regulations resulting in the prolonged stay in operationalization of the SecretariatThe NRA mandate came to an end on 31 April 2022 by lapse of time as per the NRA Act 2019 resulting in the dissolution of the NRA without a clear transitional arrangement. This was accompanied by litigation that caused delay in processing outstanding work

title.narrative: UNDAF Outcome 1: By 2023, government and nongovernmental institutions deliver their mandates and uphold good governance, rule of law, and human rights, with all people having improved access to justice and participating in social and political decisionmaking processes in a peaceful environment.

description.narrative: The UNDP, through intervention in collaboration with the European Union, UN, Civil Society, Faith based Organisations, together with development partners, contributed to Lesothos progress in strengthening governance, rule of law, human rights, access to justice and peace and stability in the country. Lesothos ranking in the Democracy Index has slightly decreased to 63 in 2021 (baseline in 2017: 56) indicating further need for the improvement. Over 50 percent of the recommendations and action points from the National Dialogue and reform process were implemented (baseline in 2017: 0 percent) and Lesothos score on Governance Index has improved to 82.2 (baseline in 2017: 54.5). Finally, Lesotho conducted a peaceful, credible and transparent election in October 2022 declared free and fair by the European Union, African Union, Southern African Development Community and United Kingdom observation missions and peaceful transition of power has proved Lesothos maturity in democracy for the first time in its history

title.narrative: Proportion of reform recommendations addressing persons with disabilities, womens empowerment, and gender equality adopted

description.narrative: Proportion of reform recommendations addressing persons with disabilities, womens empowerment, and gender equality adopted

comment.narrative: Progress During the reporting period significant progress was achieved towards the attainment of the Output targets. Through technical support policy advisory and highlevel engagement with government and stakeholders the 11th Amendment to the Constitution Act 2022 was approved by Cabinet passed by Parliament and Assented to by the King. Although this was later annulled by the courts it remains a significant milestone in Lesothos transformation into a stable nation. The Constitutional Amendment is also accompanied by 36 legislations in seven thematic sectors Constitutional Parliamentary Security Justice Public Service Economic and Media Reforms httpswww.gov.lsleadersapplaudpassingofeleventhamendmentofconsitution. title.narrative: Percentage of peace committees that integrate gender consideration in their negotiations

description.narrative: Percentage of peace committees that integrate gender consideration in their negotiations

comment.narrative: Progress The capacity of local actors was strengthened resulting in conflict mitigation. The Peaceful national election of October 2022 is partly attributed to this support where the UN contributed through the training of 35 women from political Parties and women leaders within and out of parliament on conflict prevention and mediation and their role in intraparty democracy and conflict prevention and mitigation. Community Peace and security was enhanced at local level through pilot Ribaneng Peace committee Initiative. The Committee benefited from conflict mediation training and integration of youth as peace agents. Training of Youth Peace Committees in both the southern district of Mafteng and the Northern district of Botha Bothe was carried out for over 100 youth participants by end 2022. Additionally the Lehokela community policing app being scaled up across select community to enhance interaction and reporting for community policing. Challenges 2022 being an election year the citizens and public officials were focused on the national elections and political campaigns which negatively impacted programme traction. Some of the activities that required active participation of political leadership were shelved due to the election fever.While there are numerous efforts underway to transform the conflict in the local communities existing capacity and infrastructure do not seem to match the scale and magnitude of the effort required in light of the challenges that need to be addressed. Experience from the pilot districts indicate a lack capacity for uptake as well as the infrastructures for peace to achieve sustainable peace. This requires local and national actors to play a leading role.

Progress under the Output 1.3 were significantly affected by lack of funding. There was prolonged negotiations with the donors leading to delay in the disbusrement of funds. Whereas UNDP had agreed to prefinance the Contribution Agreement the limited funds from UNDP own resources could not sufficiently cover the planned expenditures for a prolonged period. The limited funds were diverted to priority activities particularly finalization of the time bound legislation .The second constrained emanated from the delayed enactment of the 11th Amendment to the Constitution Act and supplementary legislations. Through civic education public forums and ICT platforms Civil Society FaithBased Groups Womenled organizations youth the elderly and people with disabilities were to empower the citizens to monitor implementation of the Constitutional Amendments and report progress or lack thereof for remediation action. With the annulment of the Act by the court these activities were suspended for subsequent period.

comment.narrative: Progress The capacity of local actors was strengthened resulting in conflict mitigation. The Peaceful national election of October 2022 is partly attributed to this support where the UN contributed through the training of 35 women from political Parties and women leaders within and out of parliament on conflict prevention and mediation and their role in intraparty democracy and conflict prevention and mitigation. Community Peace and security was enhanced at local level through pilot Ribaneng Peace committee Initiative. The Committee benefited from conflict mediation training and integration of youth as peace agents. Training of Youth Peace Committees in both the southern district of Mafteng and the Northern district of Botha Bothe was carried out for over 100 youth participants by end 2022. Additionally the Lehokela community policing app being scaled up across select community to enhance interaction and reporting for community policing. Challenges 2022 being an election year the citizens and public officials were focused on the national elections and political campaigns which negatively impacted programme traction. Some of the activities that required active participation of political leadership were shelved due to the election fever.While there are numerous efforts underway to transform the conflict in the local communities existing capacity and infrastructure do not seem to match the scale and magnitude of the effort required in light of the challenges that need to be addressed. Experience from the pilot districts indicate a lack capacity for uptake as well as the infrastructures for peace to achieve sustainable peace. This requires local and national actors to play a leading role.

Progress under the Output 1.3 were significantly affected by lack of funding. There was prolonged negotiations with the donors leading to delay in the disbusrement of funds. Whereas UNDP had agreed to prefinance the Contribution Agreement the limited funds from UNDP own resources could not sufficiently cover the planned expenditures for a prolonged period. The limited funds were diverted to priority activities particularly finalization of the time bound legislation .The second constrained emanated from the delayed enactment of the 11th Amendment to the Constitution Act and supplementary legislations. Through civic education public forums and ICT platforms Civil Society FaithBased Groups Womenled organizations youth the elderly and people with disabilities were to empower the citizens to monitor implementation of the Constitutional Amendments and report progress or lack thereof for remediation action. With the annulment of the Act by the court these activities were suspended for subsequent period.

comment.narrative: Progress Through sustained technical support policy advisory and financial support the role of Civil Society FaithBased Groups Womenled organizations youth the elderly people with disabilities and other special interest groups as alternative voices of the citizens and social leaders in Lesotho has been amplified and centerstaged in national policy processes. This is illustrated by the institutionalization of representation of these groups in key reform legislation as proposed in the 11th Amendment to the Constitution Act and draft supplementary legislations. Previously these groups would participate in national policy processes by invitation this has however been reversed and anchored in law.Civil Society FaithBased Groups Womenled organizations youth the elderly and people with disabilities have become strategic partners and key players in consensus building and convening national leaders to address matters of national concern. Through UNDP support these groups convened the First consultative process on the 11th Amendment to the Constitution Bill bringing together the National Assembly and Senate resulting in bipartisan agreement on contentious issues. Through this deadlockbreaking mechanism parliament was recalled on an exceptional basis resulting in subsequent enactment of the Act.In collaboration with the Christian Council of Lesotho all political parties agreed and signed a preelection pledge committing to comply with prevailing electoral laws code of conduct and peaceful elections. The independent observer groups partly attributed to the peaceful election and accepting of the outcome to the prior commitment of the political parties.Challenges Progress under the indicator were significantly affected by lack of funding. There was prolonged negotiations with the donors leading to delay in the disbursement of funds. Whereas UNDP had agreed to prefinance the Contribution Agreement the limited funds from UNDP own resources could not sufficiently cover the planned expenditures for a prolonged period. The limited funds were diverted to priority activities particularly finalization of the time bound legislation .The second constrained emanated from the delayed enactment of the 11th Amendment to the Constitution Act and supplementary legislations. Through civic education public forums and ICT platforms Civil Society FaithBased Groups Womenled organizations youth the elderly and people with disabilities were to empower the citizens to monitor implementation of the Constitutional Amendments and report progress or lack thereof for remediation action. With the annulment of the Act by the court these activities were suspended for subsequent period

title.narrative: Country score on the Economist Intelligence Units Democracy Index

description.narrative: The Democracy Index is based on five categories: electoral process and pluralism; civil liberties; the functioning of government; political participation; and political culture. It provides a snapshot of the state of democracy for 165 independent states, which make up the majority of the worlds states (microstates are excluded). There is both an overall score as well as scores in individual categories. Based on their scores on a range of indicators within these categories, each country is then itself categorised as one of four types of regime: full democracies; flawed democracies; hybrid regimes; and authoritarian regimes.

The outlook for political stability is good and the new government will benefit from a honeymoon period this year. Although social frustrations are likely owing largely to high domestic prices and limited economic opportunities we do not forecast any widespread unrest in 2023. A decline in receipts from the Southern African Customs Union will put pressure on the governments fiscal position which we expect to improve although the budget will remain in deficit with a shortfall equivalent to 6.2 of GDP in 2023 down from 9.3 of GDP in 2022. The external position will deteriorate in 2023 as the currentaccount deficit widens to 9.9 of GDP from 8.8 of GDP in 2022 as imports remain expensive and export earnings dip in line with declining global prices for diamonds.

Lesothos ranking in the Democracy Index has slightly decreased to 63 in 2021 (baseline in 2017: 56) indicating further need for the improvement. Over 50 percent of the recommendations and action points from the National Dialogue and reform process were implemented (baseline in 2017: 0 percent) and Lesothos score on Governance Index has improved to 82.2 (baseline in 2017: 54.5). Finally, Lesotho conducted a peaceful, credible and transparent election in October 2022 declared free and fair by the European Union, African Union, Southern African Development Community and United Kingdom observation missions and peaceful transition of power has proved Lesothos maturity in democracy for the first time in its history

title.narrative: Country score on the Economist Intelligence Units Democracy Index

description.narrative: The Democracy Index is based on five categories: electoral process and pluralism; civil liberties; the functioning of government; political participation; and political culture. It provides a snapshot of the state of democracy for 165 independent states, which make up the majority of the worlds states (microstates are excluded). There is both an overall score as well as scores in individual categories. Based on their scores on a range of indicators within these categories, each country is then itself categorised as one of four types of regime: full democracies; flawed democracies; hybrid regimes; and authoritarian regimes.

comment.narrative: The UNDP through intervention in collaboration with the European Union UN Civil Society Faith based Organisations together with development partners contributed to Lesothos progress in strengthening governance rule of law human rights access to justice and peace and stability in the country. Lesothos ranking in the Democracy Index has slightly decreased to 63 in 2021 baseline in 2017 56 indicating further need for the improvement. Over 50 percent of the recommendations and action points from the National Dialogue and reform process were implemented baseline in 2017 0 percent and Lesothos score on Governance Index has improved to 82.2 baseline in 2017 54.5. Finally Lesotho conducted a peaceful credible and transparent election in October 2022 declared free and fair by the European Union African Union Southern African Development Community and United Kingdom observation missions and peaceful transition of power has proved Lesothos maturity in democracy for the first time in its history

The outlook for political stability is good and the new government will benefit from a honeymoon period this year. Although social frustrations are likely owing largely to high domestic prices and limited economic opportunities we do not forecast any widespread unrest in 2023. A decline in receipts from the Southern African Customs Union will put pressure on the governments fiscal position which we expect to improve although the budget will remain in deficit with a shortfall equivalent to 6.2 of GDP in 2023 down from 9.3 of GDP in 2022. The external position will deteriorate in 2023 as the currentaccount deficit widens to 9.9 of GDP from 8.8 of GDP in 2022 as imports remain expensive and export earnings dip in line with declining global prices for diamonds.

title.narrative: Proportion of reform recommendations addressing persons with disabilities, womens empowerment, and gender equality implemented

description.narrative: Proportion of reform recommendations addressing persons with disabilities, womens empowerment, and gender equality implemented

comment.narrative: Through policy technical and operational support to processes mechanisms and strategies necessary to enhance women participation national assembly and local governments the proportion of women representation increased by 25 Home IEC Lesotho Parliament of Lesotho. Technical support to women parliamentary caucus and training of women candidates improved the capacity of women to organize and campaign for electoral processes resulting in an increase of 25 women through direct election httpsgenderlinks.org.zanewslesothocelebratingnewdawnalthoughgenderequalityremainselusive. The number of women elected on Proportional Representation was increased to 15. The most significant achievements in promoting women participation in legislative and executive leadership positions with females constituting 33 of the Cabinet www.gov.ls. The increased number of women in the legislature and executive decisionmaking will have a multiplier effect on the general level of public sector effectiveness and accountability in a country. This is particularly pertinent as the country seeks to respond and recover from the impact of COVID19

1.Prolonged debate and discussions at the NRA Plenary as well as the need to reach a consensus on contentious issues resulted in an extended stay of processing and finalization of bills policies and strategies. Subsequently the bills strategies and policies could not be presented to Parliament for enactment and implementation as per the Action targets. This further impacted on completion of activities policy sequencing and costing exercises that are dependent on the enactment of laws policies and strategies. The collapse of the 10th Amendment to the Constitution Bill 2022 altered the implementation arrangement of activities related to the implementation of the reforms.
