title.narrative: No. of citizen forums on reforms and good governance facilitated by nonstate actors

description.narrative: No. of citizen forums on reforms and good governance facilitated by nonstate actors

comment.narrative: To enhance citizen participation in national processes UNDP in collaboration with key stakeholders generated key priorities for capacity development that will improve citizen engagement in the implementation of the national reforms httpswww.undp.org. The consensus building process led by the CSOs resulted in agreement at the Senate and National Assembly leading to passage of the 11th Constitutional Amendment through extraordinary recall of parliament under State of Emergency provisions. Though the process was nullified by the Court it remains a significant progress towards adoption of the nationally agreed reforms as a legal instrument for implementation.

Preparatory work for convening the First HighLevel Forum on Implementation of Lesotho National Reforms geared towards adequately informing stakeholders and the Basotho public about national reforms implementation process provide space for national reflection and forward looking were initiated. These included conceptualization of the Forum securing venue developing communication and visibility materials and securing high level political concurrence on the public value and legitimacy of the event.

Over 50 percent of the recommendations and action points from the National Dialogue and reform process were implemented (baseline in 2017: 0 percent) and Lesothos score on Governance Index has improved to 82.2 (baseline in 2017: 54.5). Finally, Lesotho conducted a peaceful, credible and transparent election in October 2022 declared free and fair by the European Union, African Union, Southern African Development Community and United Kingdom observation missions and peaceful transition of power has proved Lesothos maturity in democracy for the first time in its history

title.narrative: No. of citizen forums on reforms and good governance facilitated by nonstate actors

description.narrative: No. of citizen forums on reforms and good governance facilitated by nonstate actors

comment.narrative: To enhance citizen participation in national processes UNDP in collaboration with key stakeholders generated key priorities for capacity development that will improve citizen engagement in the implementation of the national reforms httpswww.undp.org. The consensus building process led by the CSOs resulted in agreement at the Senate and National Assembly leading to passage of the 11th Constitutional Amendment through extraordinary recall of parliament under State of Emergency provisions. Though the process was nullified by the Court it remains a significant progress towards adoption of the nationally agreed reforms as a legal instrument for implementation.

Preparatory work for convening the First HighLevel Forum on Implementation of Lesotho National Reforms geared towards adequately informing stakeholders and the Basotho public about national reforms implementation process provide space for national reflection and forward looking were initiated. These included conceptualization of the Forum securing venue developing communication and visibility materials and securing high level political concurrence on the public value and legitimacy of the event.

title.narrative: 4: Efficient and effective information, education and communication for reforms implementation

description.narrative: The output will maximise the role of information, education and communication in reform processes through strategic communication for coalition building and influencing attitudes, public opinion and behaviour change. It will seek to increase the success and sustainability of agreed reforms by addressing political barriers in the form of lack of political will among key government leaders, vested interests, lack of citizen demand for accountability, or hostile public opinion. Shortcomings in coordinated messaging and communication during the dialogue phase appeared to have slowed to some extent the process of consensus building and prolonged negotiations especially at high political leadership. Therefore, the output will support realisation of early political buyin and acceleration of reforms implementation. This will be key to translating reform objectives into achieving the desired results on the ground. Equally important will be alignment of citizens, stakeholders, and by linking the constitutive elements of the public sphere engaged citizenries, vibrant civil societies, plural and independent media systems, and open government institutions to facilitate the national reforms implementation to shape informed public opinion. It shall influence the opinions, attitudes and ultimately the behaviour of key stakeholders including leaders, bureaucrats, and citizens to increase stakeholders support for the reform objectives and enhance citizen engagement in political systems. The Government, NRA and CSOs capacity for effective information, economic and communication with direct support embedded in them

title.narrative: Proportion of 2,000,000 population reached by information, communication and education programmes

description.narrative: Proportion of 2,000,000 population reached by information, communication and education programmes

comment.narrative: Limited progress was achieved in the specific activity owing to limited funding from prefinancing facility. However communication messages and public awareness programmes were developed ready for production and dissemination. Key activities completed include1.Radio and TV campaign programme was developed and adopted for implementation with regular TV appearances by NRA Members and Secretariat.2.Flyers brochures burner billboards and branded stationary were designed awaiting reproduction and dissemination.3.Regular newspaper articles and paid advertisements were generated and disseminated in the weekly publications.Challenge1 The activities under the output were significantly affected by lack of funding. Whereas UNDP had agreed to prefinance the Contribution Agreement the limited funds could not sufficiently cover the planned expenditures for a prolonged period. The limited funds were diverted to priority activities particularly salaries emoluments and equipment for the NRA Secretariat.2 In October 2022 a decision to suspend the Action following the court decision on the 10th Amendment to the Constitution Bill 2022 altered the implementation arrangement of activities to Design develop and execute citizen awareness and public information programmes on implementation of reforms could not be sustained in the form and shape envisaged in the programme design.

The Annual Output targets were partially Based on extrapolation of viewership radio tune and visits to public malls where advertisement were run an estimated reach of 9 was achieved to be ascertained by a perception survey in March 2022. Key milestones achieved include1.Conceptualization design development and approval by NRA Plenary of the public information and communication campaign programme.2.Sustained radio and TV programmes as well as social media activities on national reforms by NRA members and secretariat. This was complimented by and routine advertisement in malls and road side mega screens. A public perception survey will be undertaken in March 2022 to determine the understanding and reach for the year ending 31 October 2021.3.Monthly public debates on TV call in radio talk shows were sustained with an estimated 9 reach to the total population. Conclusive results shall be confirmed with a public perception survey in March 2022. March 2022 is purposively identified to coincide with the High Level Forum on Implementation of Reforms that is expected to have a broad cross section of stakeholders local and SADC over a period of 3 days

title.narrative: 4: Efficient and effective information, education and communication for reforms implementation

It shall influence the opinions, attitudes and ultimately the behaviour of key stakeholders including leaders, bureaucrats, and citizens to increase stakeholders support for the reform objectives and enhance citizen engagement in political systems. The Government, NRA and CSOs capacity for effective information, economic and communication with direct support embedded in them

title.narrative: 2.0 Improved democratic governance and economic performance through targeted shortterm legal, policy and institutional reforms in the Constitutional sector; Justice sector; Parliamentary sector; Economic sector; Public service sector; Security sector; Media sector.

description.narrative: The proposed Output will aggregate prioritised objectives to guide coordinated reforms implementation in the seven thematic sectors. This will entail creation of a mechanism for realistic, sequencing and coherent implementations of reforms. The output will also support proper management of the reforms implementation process through effective and coherent leadership; establishment of a clear strategic framework for prioritisation of reforms and realistic planning of their implementation. It shall also ensure financial sustainability of reforms and holistic management of decisionmaking process. Specifically policy analysis, costing, prioritising, drafting legislations/policies and sequencing implementation of shortterm, catalytic reforms in the seven thematic sectors namely shall be executed.

title.narrative: No of laws, policies and institutional reforms formulated

description.narrative: No of laws, policies and institutional reforms formulated

comment.narrative: The annual output targets were exceeded where 36 pieces of legislation and constitutional amendments were processed by NRA submitted to the Minister of Law and Justice approved by cabinet and tabled in parliament through the Omnibus Bill. The Omnibus Bill went through the first reading and presented to the Parliamentary Portfolio Committee for scrutiny. The results are summarized as follows1.The National Reforms Authority prioritized the adoption of Constitutional Amendments in five thematic sectors in the form of Omnibus Bill Eleventh Constitutional Amendment Bill for provisions that require a simple majority vote in Parliament. Apart from the Omnibus Bill the Authority processed and forwarded the following draft Bill coupled with some of the Media Sector Regulatory instruments to Government for onward transmission to Parliament Referendum Bill Media Policy and Media Code of Conduct. The Eleventh Constitutional Amendment Bill comprised amendments in the following thematic sectors Constitutional Reforms Parliamentary Reforms Justice Sector Reforms Security Sector Reforms and Public Sector Reforms.2.Constitutional Reforms related amendments address the number of Ministers preamble to the constitution office of the Prime Minister and Deputy PM pensions and age of Majority 3.Parliamentary Reforms related amendments address floor Crossing Formation of Coalition Government Impeachment of the sitting Prime Minister Sessions of Parliament and Prorogation and Dissolution of Parliament.4.Security Sector Reforms related amendments address Mandates of Security Agencies Establishment of National Security Commission Establishment of the Code of Conduct Establishment of National Security Council Appointments and removal of Security Chiefs Restrictions on Political Activism and Protection from Political Interference and Development of National Security Policy.5.Justice Sector Reforms related amendments address Independence and Prosecutorial Powers of Director of Corruption and Economic Crimes and establishment of the Human Rights Commission.6.Public Sector Reforms related amendments seeks to reform the Office of Head of Civil Service Government Secretary Secretary to Cabinet and offices of Permanent Secretaries.7.Economic Sector Reforms related amendments address the Consolidated Fund Authorization of Expenditure from the Consolidated Fund by Appropriation Authorization of Expenditure in advance of Appropriation Public Debt the office of Auditor General and Contingencies Fund.8.The 10th Amendment to the Constitution Constitutional Bill 2022 containing 98 proposals in the seven thematic sectors was approved by Cabinet Tabled in Parliament submitted to the relevant Portfolio Committee and approved by Plenary of the House for onward transmission to Senate for Double entrenched amendments.9.The Action supported the Senate through technical working session on the 10th Constitutional Amendment Bill 2022 resulting in a deeper understanding of the bill and fasttracking debate on it in a record 2 days.10.During the reporting period significant progress was achieved towards the attainment of the Output targets. Through technical support policy advisory and highlevel engagement with government and stakeholders the 10th Amendment to the Constitution Act 2022 was approved by Cabinet passed by Parliament and Assented to by the King. Although this was later annulled by the courts it remains a significant milestone in Lesothos transformation into a stable nation. The Constitutional Amendment is also accompanied by 36 legislations in seven thematic sectors Constitutional Parliamentary Security Justice Public Service Economic and Media Reforms httpswww.gov.lsleadersapplaudpassingofeleventhamendmentofconsitution.

title.narrative: No of laws, policies and institutional reforms implementation initiated

description.narrative: No of laws, policies and institutional reforms implementation initiated

comment.narrative: 1 Prolonged debate and discussions at the NRA Plenary as well as the need to reach consensus on contentious issues resulted in extended stay of processing and finalization of bills policies and strategies. Subsequently the bills strategies and policies could not be presented to Parliament for enactment and implementation as per the Action targets. This further impacted on completion of activities policy sequencing and costing exercises that are dependent on enactment of laws policies and strategies.2 Conflicting interests among stakeholders and political leadership impacted on the speed to reach consensus and bipartisan agreements on contentious reforms issues leading to prolonged debate.3 The resignation of two technical staff also caused a variance in the number of personnel required to be maintained at post by the Secretariat.4 There was prolonged negotiations on the Terms and Conditions of Service of the NRA Secretariat resulting in nonimplementation of activities related to capacity building of civil service staff undertaking of analysis and policy studies5 There was prolonged debate political posturing and changes in the leadership of the Portfolio Committee leading to delay in processing of the Bill that was eventually stalled by Sine Die adjournment of parliament.6 In October 2022 a decision to suspend the Action following the court decision on the 10th Amendment to the Constitution Bill 2022 altered the implementation arrangement of activities related to the maintenance of staff at post.7 Whereas a request to extend support to the National Reforms Transitional Office was advanced in May 2022 the nonpassage of the 10th Amendment to the Constitution Bill 2022 meant that the proposed activities such as enabling legislations and establishments of new institutions proposed in the Amendment could not be legally implemented.

This further impacted on completion of activities policy sequencing and costing exercises that are dependent on enactment of laws policies and strategies.2 Conflicting interests among stakeholders and political leadership impacted on the speed to reach consensus and bipartisan agreements on contentious reforms issues leading to prolonged debate.3 The resignation of two technical staff also caused a variance in the number of personnel required to be maintained at post by the Secretariat.4 There was prolonged negotiations on the Terms and Conditions of Service of the NRA Secretariat resulting in nonimplementation of activities related to capacity building of civil service staff undertaking of analysis and policy studies5 There was prolonged debate political posturing and changes in the leadership of the Portfolio Committee leading to delay in processing of the Bill that was eventually stalled by Sine Die adjournment of parliament.

title.narrative: 2.0 Improved democratic governance and economic performance through targeted shortterm legal, policy and institutional reforms in the Constitutional sector; Justice sector; Parliamentary sector; Economic sector; Public service sector; Security sector; Media sector.

description.narrative: The proposed Output will aggregate prioritised objectives to guide coordinated reforms implementation in the seven thematic sectors. This will entail creation of a mechanism for realistic, sequencing and coherent implementations of reforms. The output will also support proper management of the reforms implementation process through effective and coherent leadership; establishment of a clear strategic framework for prioritisation of reforms and realistic planning of their implementation. It shall also ensure financial sustainability of reforms and holistic management of decisionmaking process. Specifically policy analysis, costing, prioritising, drafting legislations/policies and sequencing implementation of shortterm, catalytic reforms in the seven thematic sectors namely shall be executed.
